描述_ZN: Song Stepping" scroll, Southern Song Dynasty, by Ma Yuan, on silk, color, 192.5 cm long, 111 cm wide.　　"It is a very old custom in the countryside of southern China that when the villagers have worked hard for a year and finally have a good harvest, the whole village, men, women and children, step to the beat, sing and dance, celebrating the harvest and thanking nature for its bounty, just as happily and lively as the New Year festival.　　On the surface, the painting looks like a landscape painting showing the natural landscape, but in reality it is a customary painting depicting human life. The author, Ma Yuan, has arranged a few pointillist figures in the picture so that the theme of the painting can be fully displayed. Instead of depicting the whole picture of the countryside singing scene, the painter has chosen a few very representative figures of the villagers: a middle-aged villager, who has drunk a few bowls of wine out of joy, stumbles, staggers and is drunk, but the gourd holding the wine is not forgotten and is still properly carried on his shoulder; an old man with a white beard, who has also drunk a lot of wine, has one hand on a crutch and the other hand raised high, with his feet off the ground and his hands dancing. Feet off the ground, hands dancing, unusual excitement. Their demeanor is not in line with their age, so they seem particularly comical and ridiculous. After depicting the adults, Ma Yuan felt that it was not enough to express the joyful and indulgent atmosphere, so he specially arranged two young children, male and female, in the lower left corner of the painting, who turn around and stare at their elders with astonished eyes, why is the usual parental bullying and majesty gone? The older girl, who also covered her mouth with her hand, was secretly laughing. These two groups of characters echo each other and set each other off, pushing the joyful and happy mood of the "song" to the extreme. However, if we look closely at the picture, the author has only drawn six people, but he has managed to render the atmosphere so well. From these six villagers, one can fully feel the singing, the beat of the ground and the laughter coming from the whole village. Ma Yuan's artistic expression of "taking one for ten" and "seeing the big with the small" is really brilliant.　　A few figures occupy a small place in the picture, but they are the most striking. The lines of the figures are strong and vigorous, and their dynamics are lively and interesting, all showing Ma Yuan's extraordinary skills.　　Ma Yuan's method of painting the mountains and rocks is also extremely distinctive. He used the side sweep of the brush to express the steepness of the mountains and the texture of the hard rocks, which are as if they were split by a giant axe. Ma Yuan also innovated in the composition of his paintings. He liked to concentrate the rocks in the picture on a certain corner to form a contrast between reality and fiction, which gave him the name "Ma Yijiao," although this feature is not very obvious in this work. Ma Yuan also had his own habit of painting trees. He often drew the branches of the trees diagonally downward, so some people summarized it into four words: "dragging branches and Ma Yuan".　　On the top of Ma Yuan's painting "Stepping on a Song", there is a five-line poem, which was copied from a poem by Wang Anshi of the Northern Song Dynasty by Emperor Ningzong of the Southern Song Dynasty. The poem reads, "The rain is clear, the sun is shining, the city is beautiful, the people are happy in the year of plenty, and the song is on the monastery." This is the Southern Song emperor's wish for a peaceful and prosperous world, and the painter Ma Yuan, who served the court, painted with this poem as the title.
